global_rules.source_affordance: Expose source ID, publisher, URL, locator, access date, year/period, geography, unit, boundary, and caveat for every mark.
global_rules.metric_labels: Withdrawal, consumptive use, delivery, capacity, and indirect footprint require different visual encodings and may not share an unlabeled axis.
global_rules.dates: Every future value must be labeled regulatory deadline, planning counterfactual, infrastructure target, or scenario/model.
global_rules.nulls: Unknown values remain null; do not convert to zero or interpolate.
global_rules.volatility: Current drought stages, reservoir levels, and restrictions require a fetched timestamp and stale-data warning.
global_rules.geography: National averages may not be used as facility or watershed impact estimates.

charts.title: U.S. water withdrawals by category and source
constraints: Categories shown do not sum exactly to total because mining and aquaculture are absent in early years and reporting categories changed.
Mark 2015 as the last fully comparable national inventory; do not extend the line to 2026.

charts.title: Withdrawal is not consumption
constraints: Use 2010–20 conterminous-U.S. values only.
Do not mix 2015 national values into the same bars.

charts.title: Drinking water is a small part of household service
constraints: State that WHO references are basic-needs guidance and 82 gpcd is a U.S. average.
Never imply that a drinking-only device replaces household water service.

charts.title: Groundwater-dependent agriculture faces a staggered transition
constraints: Map only source-provided spatial data.
Label Hale County as one official planning case, not the whole High Plains aquifer.
Do not use 'aquifer empty by 2100'.

charts.title: Data-center water is nationally small and locally concentrated
constraints: Keep direct and indirect water separate.
Do not map national averages to facilities.
Facility map requires verified campus location, water source, seasonal consumption, and utility context.

charts.title: Where plastics affect freshwater
constraints: Do not show a national savings total until product-service counterfactual datasets are populated.
Water quantity, quality, and scarcity require separate indicators.

charts.title: How selected U.S. cities obtain water
constraints: Do not shade city-wide run-out probability.
Use dated mixes only for the source year.
Hover text must repeat each critical qualification.

charts.title: When freshwater risks can manifest
constraints: Use distinct shapes and labels for every risk type.
Open-ended hazards cannot be assigned a fabricated year.
Planning counterfactuals must show the avoided-if-strategies-built note.

charts.title: Why coastal wells become saline
constraints: Sea level must not be the only incoming cause.
Add place-specific pathways for Miami, Long Island, and Brunswick.

charts.title: Desalination works at municipal increments; national replacement is enormous
constraints: Call plant counts capacity-equivalents.
Energy range excludes distribution and other stated items.
Do not imply all current freshwater must be replaced.

charts.title: Atmospheric water generation: drinking niche versus utility scale
constraints: Label ENERGY STAR values as a condenser proxy, not certified AWG performance.
Show humidity/temperature derating and potable-treatment requirements adjacent to the chart.
Use logarithmic axes where needed.

charts.title: Match the intervention to the water problem
constraints: Score reliability, energy, cost, water quality, ecosystem, equity, and implementation time separately.
No universal technology winner.
